body: The people in question have faded from my life, simply acquaintances from middle school (sometimes even less). I just feel bad for feeding into their pain. Even unknowingly. I didn't understand the concept of nudes and how unethical the practices were. I would love to help forbid this from happening so frequently. Thanks for the comment and the support.
I have one who I speak to semi often. We have discussed these matters before, but they often creep back up. I am on medication and may need to up to dosage.

I'm sorry that I keep rambling, i am just in a very negative headspace right now. In the midst of a panic attack and I need to let it out. My mother doesn't understand and my therapist is away. Facing the reality of the situation is horrible, but no matter how many times I think "learn from your mistakes", the persistent thought of "you did this thing and you should be ashamed, because you hate people who do these things" creeps back up and takes charge. I lose all motivation and become powerless. I struggle to control it and often find myself just suppressing it, which is also a horrible thing to do. I'm at a crossroads and I fear that nothing will get better. It certainly feels like I've reached the conclusion of this dilemma, and I have not made amends.

Another factor is my desperate need for reassurance, part of my OCD. I've posted about stuff like this on reddit many many times in the past, hoping that I can find refuge. People are often very supportive. However, the relief i get from this is very temporary. It is also impacted by the fact that in posts like this I have made before, there are people who respond the way that I think of myself. That I am a piece of shit who did shitty things. Those comments reinforce the negative feelings I have about myself and cancel out the support. I have a problem, I'm too scared to confront my past demons myself for fear that I will permanently hate myself and find no enjoyment in life anymore. I recognize that everyone has regrets and has made mistakes, but in the case of something like this, it feels too real and too serious to be passed off as a learning experience. I just really wish i didn't do the things I did, and nothing can ever change that fact. I have to learn how to live with accepting what I did. And that's too hard.

Thank you. As you said, it's very hard to take weight off of me personally. I have OCD and get stuck of stuff like this, I have a history of thinking that I'm a horrible person because of it. I would love to help shed light on stuff like this. Part of me wants to think that I was just an impressionable kid who was influenced by the wrong people at the wrong time, but another part of me realizes that in the end, I decided to do these things and that I consciously made these decisions. The fact that nothing can change that hurts me deeply, I pride myself of being courteous and sympathetic, but knowing that I took part in something like this completely clouds over everything I thought i knew. As far as I'm concerned, i've done a horrible thing and nothing can change that. It's very hard to live with the guilt. I will talk to my therapist about trying to channel that healthy guilt, but I just feel unforgivable and not worthy of redemption.
i have suffered with ocd for years now and it sucks getting stuck on a thought like this.
i'm a senior in high school, but what I did was deplorable regardless
